claim: Grand Palace is open daily 8:30 AM-4:30 PM with tickets sold 8:30 AM-3:30 PM; foreigner entry is 500 baht and includes Wat Phra Kaew plus the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles; sleeveless tops, shorts, torn or tight pants, mini skirts, and see-through tops are prohibited.
quote: 500 baht for Foreigners. Inclusive of access to Wat Phra Kaew and Queen Sirikit Museum of Textile

claim: Wat Pho costs 300 baht (free for children under 120 cm) and is open 8:00 AM-6:30 PM; Wat Arun is 200 baht, open 8:30 AM-6:00 PM with last tickets at 5:40 PM; Wat Saket costs 100 baht to climb the mount; Wat Traimit is 100 baht for the Buddha plus 100 baht for the museum.
quote: Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha) 300 Baht per person ... Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) 200 Baht per person ... Wat Saket (Golden Mount) 100 Baht per person

claim: Wat Pho's entry fee rose to 300 baht on 1 January 2024 (previously 200 baht).
quote: As of January 1, 2024, the fee increased to 300 Baht

claim: At Wat Arun in 2026, climbing is restricted to the first terrace level of the central prang, but that level still delivers panoramic views of the Chao Phraya River and the Grand Palace skyline.
quote: Climbing is restricted to the first terrace level as of 2026, which still delivers panoramic views of the Chao Phraya River and the Grand Palace skyline

claim: MOCA Bangkok admission is 300 baht for adults, 120 baht for students, and free for under-13s, seniors over 60, people with disabilities, and priests; hours are Tuesday-Sunday 10 AM-6 PM, closed Mondays.
quote: Adult: 300 baht ... Student (with ID): 120 baht ... Tuesday - Sunday 10.00 am - 06.00 pm (Closed on Mondays)

claim: Jim Thompson House charges 250 baht for adults and 150 baht for ages 10-21, with free entry for children under 10; the museum is open 10:00 AM-5:00 PM daily and tours run every 20-30 minutes in multiple languages.
quote: Entrance fee is 250 baht (~$7.64) for adults, 150 baht (~$4.59) for children between 10-21 years old and free entry for children under 10

claim: Travel writer Robert Schrader explicitly recommends against the Grand Palace for many visitors, calling the admission price 'insane,' citing year-round crowds, and arguing the site 'isn't that much more beautiful' than other Bangkok temples; he points clients to Wat Pho and Wat Arun instead.
quote: The price of admission to the Grand Palace is insane ... I often recommend against my private travel clients visiting the Grand Palace

claim: Wat Pho is rated one of Bangkok's best temples; the sprawling complex of 1,000+ Buddha images rewards visitors who arrive at 8 AM opening or in late afternoon to dodge midday tour-group crowds.
quote: one of Bangkok's best temples ... visiting early morning (at opening, 08:00) or late afternoon to avoid crowds and heat

claim: The best view of Wat Arun is from the east bank of the Chao Phraya River near Wat Pho pier roughly an hour before sunset; from mid-February to mid-March the sun sets almost directly behind the prang around 6:10-6:30 PM for the iconic silhouette shot.
quote: the sun sets almost directly behind Wat Arun from mid-February to mid-March, around 6:10–6:30 PM, as viewed from the east bank

claim: Wat Traimit (Temple of the Golden Buddha) is open daily 8:00 AM-5:00 PM and houses a 5.5-tonne solid-gold Buddha whose stucco coating cracked open in 1955 to reveal the gold beneath; total visit time is about an hour and best in cool morning hours.
quote: the world's largest Buddha made of solid gold weighing 5.5 tons ... In 1955, the Buddha statue (then encased in stucco) fell to the ground while being moved by workers, causing the outer layer to break and revealing the gold statue underneath

claim: MOCA Bangkok houses an 18,000 m2 space with the most comprehensive private collection of modern Thai painting and sculpture (800+ pieces); visitors are advised to allow at least 2 hours, up to 4 for enthusiasts.
quote: The 18,000 square metre space houses the most comprehensive private collection of modern painting and sculpture in Thailand, with over 800 pieces

claim: Wat Saket's Golden Mount requires a climb of about 318 steps to the gilded chedi at the summit; it is open 7:00 AM-7:00 PM with a 100-baht foreigner fee, and the rooftop chedi delivers one of Bangkok's best 360-degree panoramas.
quote: Visitors can climb the 318 steps to the top of the hill to reach the chedi and be rewarded with stunning panoramic views of Bangkok

claim: Independent reviewers rate Wat Pho and Wat Arun a 4.6/5 'worth it,' highlighting the Reclining Buddha's mother-of-pearl-inlaid feet and Wat Arun's prangs as glimpses of pre-Ayutthaya Thai architecture.
quote: the prangs identified as 'what make Wat Arun worth visiting' because they 'provide a glimpse of what the ruined prangs of Ayutthaya used to look like'
